messages:
mike_support: Hey team — customer (ACME Corp) seeing intermittent 403s on /v1/generate since yesterday evening. They say it started after they rotated a key but behavior is odd: some requests succeed, others 403 with "signature mismatch".

ingrid_support: thanks — do we have a request id for one of the failing calls? ask them for both the client-side curl and the x-rw-req-id from the response headers please.

mike_support: they sent one failing response header: x-rw-req-id: rw-req-203a7f. Also attached a truncated server log line: "auth: deny sig mismatch org=acct-123 proj=proj-alpha svckey=svc-rotated req=rw-req-203a7f"

kevin_eng: quick thought — could be org/project headers getting rewritten by their proxy or a mis-bound service key where scope is only for a different org. ask for the exact curl they used (headers included) and whether they set X-Redwood-Org / X-Redwood-Project or passed org in the token.

mike_support: forwarding their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: acct-123' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: proj-alpha' \
  -d '{"prompt":"foo"}'
```
response headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Req-Id: rw-req-203a7f
Date: Thu, 09 Feb 2035 18:12:34 GMT
```

jordan_sre: that server log line showing svckey=svc-rotated implies request reached auth service but token signature didn't match expected key. two possibilities: (1) they rotated a key but some cached gateway/proxy still uses old key for signing, (2) header canonicalization changed on the way (case/whitespace) — our signature verifier expects headers in canonical order.

ingrid_support: customer also mentions some requests were successful right after rotation then started failing again. could be a caching TTL issue. ask them to run a reproducible loop to capture both success+fail with timestamps + x-rw-req-id for each attempt.

mike_support: asked them to run: 
```
for i in {1..10}; do date -u +%s; curl -s -D - -o /dev/null \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: acct-123' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: proj-alpha' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 1; done
```

kevin_eng: also request a debug bundle: include their client request logs (full request headers), the exact token (we'll ask them to rotate after if sensitive), and a tcpdump if possible to see if intermediate proxy rewrites headers. ask them to redact secrets when posting publicly.

mike_support: customer returned two req-ids: rw-req-203a7f (fail) and rw-req-203b02 (success). attached client header dump for the failing attempt — I sanitized auth token but kept other headers: 
```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
User-Agent: curl/7.86.0
Accept: */*
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Redwood-Org: acct-123
X-Redwood-Project: proj-alpha
X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3
```

jordan_sre: can we check our ingress logs for rw-req-203a7f? I can run a tail on the ingress and auth service for that req-id to see canonicalized headers at our end.

kevin_eng: looking at auth service logs for rw-req-203a7f: 
```
2035-02-09T18:12:34.123Z auth.verify req=rw-req-203a7f svckey=svc-rotated token_kid=KID-OLD headers=[authorization,x-forwarded-for,x-redwood-org] signature_ok=false
2035-02-09T18:12:34.124Z auth.error req=rw-req-203a7f err="signature mismatch" calculated_kid=KID-NEW
```

ingrid_support: that calculated_kid=KID-NEW indicates our verifier tried to use the new key but token said KID-OLD. suggests token was minted with an old KID but our keyset currently has only the new key active, or vice versa.

mike_support: customer claims they rotated the signing key and updated the token issuer but they also have an L7 proxy that rewrites headers for multi-tenant routing. could the proxy be stripping or reordering headers needed for canonical signing?

jordan_sre: header order shouldn't affect our verifier because we parse into a map and canonicalize. but proxies sometimes drop custom headers (X-Redwood-Org) and set a different header (X-RW-Org) — if projector uses different header name, token scope check may fail because org in header doesn't match token claims. check our policy logs for claim mismatch for that req-id.

kevin_eng: policy check logs: 
```
2035-02-09T18:12:34.125Z policy.check req=rw-req-203a7f claims.org=acct-999 header.org=acct-123 -> mismatch -> deny
```

mike_support: aha — policy log shows claims.org=acct-999 while header.org=acct-123. so token was issued for acct-999 but header says acct-123. that explains signature/claim mismatch. need to confirm why their token has acct-999.

ingrid_support: ask customer: did you accidentally mint a token from another account? or are you proxying requests through a shared service that uses a different service account? also ask for the token's decoded header (they can paste base64 header only) so we can inspect the KID and sub/org claim.

mike_support: customer provided token header (base64-decoded): 
```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"KID-OLD"}
```
and token payload claims: 
```
{"sub":"svc-account","org":"acct-999","scope":"proj-beta:generate"}
```

jordan_sre: that confirms token is for acct-999. The presence of X-Redwood-Org: acct-123 in the request means the gateway is rewriting header to acct-123 while token says acct-999 => deny. So root cause is a misconfigured proxy that injects org header incorrectly.

kevin_eng: mitigation steps: 1) ask them to stop injecting X-Redwood-Org from their proxy (or align it with token org). 2) rotate the token so it matches the injected header if that's intended. 3) short-term we can allow fallback if header missing and rely on token org, but that's a policy change and requires security review (do not do automatically).

mike_support: relaying mitigation. customer says their proxy team set a default header for tenants and forgot to alter it for this service. they'll patch and retest. asked them to run the loop again and share req-ids.

ingrid_support: once they have failing req-ids, we should bundle ingress, auth, and policy logs for those req-ids and attach to the ticket. also ask them to include the proxy config snippet that sets the header.

mike_support: customer ran another test after removing default header — all 10 requests succeeded. provided rw-req ids: rw-req-204a11..rw-req-204a1a for the loop.

jordan_sre: closing note — added a short docs blurb to support about "common proxy header rewrites that cause org mismatch" and suggested a checklist: verify token org claim vs request header; capture x-rw-req-id; include proxy rewrite rules in debug bundle. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy notice — docs updated in /internal/support/runbooks (rev 11)

mike_support: marking this thread resolved, will follow up with customer to confirm post-patch monitoring. :white_check_mark:
